summary: Phase 147G implemented the standalone pcae.authority_evaluation package exactly as frozen by AEMIC-001 v1.2, the first implementation phase authorized under that contract. Built errors.py (AuthorityEvaluationError base plus eight named subclasses: InvalidClaimedIdentityError, InvalidTemplateReferenceError, MalformedDeclarationError, UnsupportedSchemaVersionError, MissingCitationTextError, TemplateIdentityMismatchError, AuthorityRegistryUnavailableError, AuthorityRegistryCorruptError); models.py (EligibleAuthorityDeclaration's closed six-field immutable shape, AuthorityEvaluationOutcome's closed eight-field immutable shape enforcing the citation_text-iff-ELIGIBLE invariant at construction time, the closed three-member EvaluationResult Enum, and the EVALUATOR_VERSION constant); registry.py (the AuthorityRegistry ABC with exactly one abstract resolve() method, zero concrete subclass); evaluation.py (the pure evaluate() function with the frozen seven-parameter signature, no Registry dependency, and the exact AEMIC-REQ-104 error-precedence ordering: template identity validity, claimed-identity validity, declaration-identity-mismatch check, evaluation_result determination, then citation_text enforcement); serialization.py (to_payload/from_payload for both record types, schema-version-first deserialization, Unicode round-trip, no digest); and __init__.py (the exact fourteen-name public re-export surface). Every mandatory AuthorityEvaluationOutcome field now has exactly one reachable, closed-input construction source for all three EvaluationResult branches including INDETERMINATE -- BF-147F.1-1's own repair, now implemented and independently exercised by test rather than merely specified in contract prose. Added 93 new tests in tests/test_phase_147g_authority_evaluation.py covering model construction/validation/immutability/equality/hashing for both record types, the closed EvaluationResult enum, all three evaluate() branches, every named malformed-input condition, template identity mismatch, four dedicated exact-error-precedence tests, determinism (including a no-side-effect-on-declaration check), the AuthorityRegistry ABC exercised through three distinct in-memory test doubles (resolvable, absent, unavailable, corrupt), serialization round-trip including Unicode and missing/null/unrecognized-value rejection, a disclosure-only public-naming audit, and a forbidden-import/package-boundary AST guard parametrized over every file in the new package. Built the field-source matrix for all nine AuthorityEvaluationOutcome fields (producing function, input source, validation, branch applicability) and a full AEMIC-REQ requirement-to-implementation-to-test coverage table, both recorded in the phase report. Added one new, isolated architecture zone declaration (authority_evaluation) to .pcae/policy.toml with zero cross-zone dependency in either direction, required only so the harness's own zone-membership machinery recognizes the new package's file paths. No concrete filesystem Registry implementation was built. No Interactive Workflow, Session, Publication Coordinator, CHGR, readiness-package, runtime, or CLI/transport integration was performed. Overall Verdict: AUTHORITY EVALUATION MODEL IMPLEMENTED. Full detail in docs/PHASE_147G_AUTHORITY_EVALUATION_MODEL_CORE_IMPLEMENTATION.md.

validation_results.name: phase_147g_error_precedence_verification
validation_results.result: TestEvaluateErrorPrecedence's four dedicated tests confirm the exact AEMIC-REQ-104/105 ordering: a malformed template_ref or claimed_identity always raises before a mismatched declaration is even inspected, and a template identity mismatch always raises before a missing-citation check on an otherwise-ELIGIBLE-shaped call -- no later-ordered check ever masks an earlier one

validation_results.name: phase_147g_determinism_verification

validation_results.name: phase_147g_serialization_verification
